what_this_is: G12's mean estimate with nothing planted (session 24, exercise 4b), authorized by Joe on 2026-11-20 (D-113). The specification is docs/gate1/simulation-spec-4b-g12-mean-estimate-2026-11-20.md (sha256 under hashes.specification). It is the mean of candidate C's headline estimate over the G12 datasets of step E's stage 2 (20,000) and stage 1 (2,000), with G11's beside it labelled as not the named figure, computed from the preserved per-dataset records of stages 1 and 2. No dataset was drawn and no stage was rerun. Every price behind the records was made up; no price was read. It is not a fresh run of G12, not a threshold, and not a change to the fuel-mix control. The plan sets no threshold for a mean away from zero and none is set here. The plan, PREANALYSIS.md, is a draft pre-analysis plan and is not frozen.
limit_read_from_the_code: In G12 the fuel shock is a national walk whose steps are normal with mean zero, loaded by the square root of a state's gas share plus a state deviation. The walk and its mirror image are equally likely, and the headline estimate is a linear function of the outcome. So the estimate's mean over datasets is zero in expectation whatever the adjustment does. A measured mean near zero is what this construction gives whether or not the linear adjustment is adequate; the mean can show a failure only if it is away from zero, and it cannot show adequacy. What bears on adequacy in these records is how the estimate moves with the realised walk (the slope on the realised change and the root-mean-square error). This is the session's reading of the code, written before any record was read.
